review_notes: I read the whole file and searched the Euler directory for repeats of its proof blocks. Most repetition inside the file is short and I did not report it: the `hK0` one-liners, the `sum_const`/`card_univ` finishes, and the Cauchy–Schwarz and `nlinarith` closings. The two induction proofs (`gradient_tame_outer_product`, `gradient_transportCommutator_word`) have different recurrences, so I did not propose a shared lemma for them. The one finding is the L²-norm-of-pointwise-dominated-field block. It appears in the target and in `OrdinaryWordBounds.jet_norm_le_word_sum`, which the target imports. Related variants also appear in `ChildParticleFieldBounds` and `GevreyProductLp`. I also noticed that `norm_le_sum_coordinates` at line 176 duplicates `EulerMeanCutoffCurl.norm_le_sum_coordinates` in `MeanCutoffCurlBound.lean`. That is a duplicate declaration rather than repeated proof machinery, so I only mention it here. Uncertainty: I have not compiled the proposed lemma. The `simp`/`simpa` details, including how `norm_jetLp` rewrites in the jet use, may need small adjustments.

findings.problem: The proof rebuilds the L² domination argument by hand. It states `hn`, which says the real eLpNorm of `‖(C j).field ·‖` equals `‖(C j).toLp‖`. It then calls `finite_domination` with `fun j x => ‖(C j).field x‖` and `fun j _ => (C j).memLp.norm`, takes `.2`, and rewrites with `field_norm` and `simp only [hn]`. `OrdinaryWordBounds.jet_norm_le_word_sum` repeats this: it defines `H w x := ‖(wordField A w).field x‖`, proves the same `hn` with `rw [field_norm,eLpNorm_norm _ ... .memLp.aestronglyMeasurable]`, calls `finite_domination ... (fun w _ => ... .memLp.norm)`, and converts with `simpa only [norm_jetLp,hn]`. Both proofs do the same thing: bound the L² norm of a function by the sum of the L² norms of finitely many smooth L² fields, given a pointwise bound by the sum of their pointwise norms. The conversion between `‖·.toLp‖` and `eLpNorm` is spelled out each time.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to `jet_norm_le_word_sum` in `OrdinaryWordBounds.lean`, which the target already imports:

`theorem eLpNorm_toReal_le_sum_fieldNorm {ι W : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup W] [NormedSpace ℝ W] (I : Finset ι) {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] (f : Space → V) (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f volume) (C : ι → SmoothL2Field W) (hdom : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, ‖(C i).field x‖) : (eLpNorm f 2 volume).toReal ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, ‖(C i).toLp‖`

Proof sketch: set `H i x := ‖(C i).field x‖`. Get `hH i _ := (C i).memLp.norm`. Apply `(finite_domination volume I f hf H hH hdom).2`. Rewrite each term with `field_norm` and `eLpNorm_norm _ (C i).memLp.aestronglyMeasurable`, using `Finset.sum_congr`.

Rewritten uses:
- `secondWord_product_gradient`: keep `hc`, then `change ‖B.toLp‖ ≤ 9*K*N; rw [field_norm]; apply (eLpNorm_toReal_le_sum_fieldNorm univ B.field B.memLp.aestronglyMeasurable C (fun x => by simp only [hc]; exact norm_le_sum_coordinates (B.field x))).trans`. The existing `calc` over `scalar_secondWord_product_gradient` then closes the goal. The local `hn` and the `finite_domination` call disappear.
- `jet_norm_le_word_sum`: `rw [norm_jetLp]; exact eLpNorm_toReal_le_sum_fieldNorm univ _ (A.integrable n).aestronglyMeasurable (wordField A) (fun x => by simpa only [wordField_field,wordDerivative,axis] using EulerSobolevDerivativeNorm.multilinear_norm_le_coordinate_sum 3 n (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n A.field x))`. The `H` definition and `hn` disappear.
findings.benefit: The measure-theoretic bookkeeping is stated once and has a name. Both call sites then show only their own mathematical content, which is the pointwise coordinate-sum domination. A future change to how `toLp` norms relate to `eLpNorm` is made in one place. The same helper could also replace the near-identical `H`/`hn`/`finite_domination` block in `ChildParticleFieldBounds` around its `hb`, with minor adaptation.
